## What it catches

A process whose version resource says it is PowerShell, the command shell, certutil, rundll32, mshta, regsvr32 or a Windows script host, while its image file has another name. Intruders rename these utilities so that rules and reviewers looking for the usual names miss them. A utility renamed to the name of another utility in the list is not caught.

```yaml
selection_orig:
  OriginalFileName:
  - PowerShell.EXE
  - Cmd.Exe
  - CertUtil.exe
  - RUNDLL32.EXE
  - MSHTA.EXE
  - REGSVR32.EXE
  - wscript.exe
  - cscript.exe
filter_name:
  Image|endswith:
  - \powershell.exe
  - \cmd.exe
  - \certutil.exe
  - \rundll32.exe
  - \mshta.exe
  - \regsvr32.exe
  - \wscript.exe
  - \cscript.exe
condition: selection_orig and not filter_name
```

## Tested on

- fires: `powershell.exe running as svchost.exe`
- fires: `cmd.exe running as update.exe`
- fires: `certutil.exe running as w.exe`
- fires: `rundll32.exe running as chrome_helper.exe`
- fires: `mshta.exe running as viewer.exe`
- fires: `regsvr32.exe running as igfx.exe`
- fires: `wscript.exe running as taskhost.exe`
- fires: `cscript.exe running as dllhost.exe`
- quiet: `powershell.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `cmd.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `certutil.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `rundll32.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `mshta.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `regsvr32.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `wscript.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `cscript.exe under its own name`
- quiet: `an ordinary program`

## False positives

- Administration bundles and portable tool kits that ship renamed copies of these utilities
- Installers that copy the command shell under a temporary name

## What it does not see

- A utility renamed to the file name of another utility of the list
- A copy whose version resource was edited or stripped
- Pipelines that do not record the original file name, such as Security event 4688

## First checks

- Read the image path and the command line: what the renamed utility was asked to do
- Find when and by what the renamed file was written
- Compare the file's hash with the system utility it claims to be
